properties.headline: Flooding under marsh vegetation is spreading at Lake Manzala
properties.subtitle: Coastal lagoon and reed beds
properties.confidence_note: Exploratory dB thresholds on L-band backscatter, not a validated flood map
properties.summary: Radar measured 2.6% of the analysed area as flooded vegetation on 12 October 2026. That is more than the 2.4% measured on 26 June 2026. causes: Water rising into standing reeds and marsh vegetation
Seasonal flooding of fish farms and marsh margins
Vegetation growing up through shallow standing water

properties.explanation:
NISAR passed over Lake Manzala 9 times between 26 June 2026 and 12 October 2026, all from the same track and look direction so the measurements can be compared. Each pass records two polarisations, HH and HV. Flooded vegetation looks very bright to radar: water and plant stems form a corner that bounces the signal straight back, while the cross-polarised signal stays weak. Pixels brighter than -5 dB in HH whose HH is more than 7 dB above their HV are counted as flooded vegetation.

Across those passes the share of the analysed area classed as flooded vegetation grew from 2.4% to 2.6%, a change of +0.2 percentage points. The lowest reading was 2.3% on 8 July 2026 and the highest 3.4% on 18 September 2026, a trend of about +0.2 percentage points per month. The outline on the map is every part of the area that was flooded vegetation in at least one month, and it covers about 11 km².

What this does not say: these are threshold rules on radar brightness, not a verified flood map. Wind roughening the water surface, wet soil after rain and a different look angle can all move the same numbers. Short, sharp changes between two passes are more likely to be weather or geometry than real change on the ground.

Why it matters: Lake Manzala is one of Egypt's largest coastal wetlands. How much of it is open water and how much is flooded marsh decides what fishing, farming and wildlife it can support. Compare with optical imagery and local water-level records before treating the change as confirmed.
